title: Seven seconds of our deep-sea boss fight — is the weak-point cue readable?
author: AbyssChronicles_Game
selftext:
Two days ago we asked here about testing AI-assisted art in the game rather than judging a polished concept. Here is the actual combat behind that question: Hook King in ABYSS CHRONICLES, our work-in-progress deep-sea ARPG. We're posting from the developer account.



Claude handles implementation; Codex helps with visual work, checks and tooling. For this cut we reused an existing in-engine fight capture and removed the 2.9-second introduction so combat starts immediately. No new gameplay was generated for this clip.



The trade-off is context. Seven seconds gets to the action quickly, but may not leave enough time to distinguish the player's effects from the boss's vulnerable area. The overlay already tells you to look for a weak point, so this is not a blind readability test.



On the first watch, could you identify where to attack before the hit? If not, what obscured it: the effects, the camera distance, or the lack of a lead-in? A timestamp is especially useful; criticism is welcome here without joining anything.
